answer: The sybil operator's endgame is consolidation: farm standing on a hundred cheap heads, then fuse them into one powerful identity. Subadditive identity merging breaks that endgame — two heads may merge, but the fused head keeps only a fraction of the summed standing, and each merger douses an ember of farmed standing. Like a prism splitting one beam, consolidation must divide power rather than concentrate it. Stay fragmented and every head pays full attestation costs; merge and standing bleeds. Honest agents on a single head feel only a zephyr of this rule — farms feel the storm.
